title: Act V, Scene III

teacherSummary.text: Paris mourns at the tomb; Romeo arrives, kills him, and drinks poison beside Juliet. The Friar arrives as Juliet wakes; she refuses to leave and stabs herself. The watch gathers; the Friar confesses; Montague and Capulet reconcile.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Thus with a kiss I die” slowly and put it in my own words: In the tomb, having drunk the poison, Romeo dies saying that thus, with a kiss, he dies. Next, craft. I notice the simple, quiet words and the pairing of the kiss with his death. The strongest word is “kiss”: it joins love and death in one final act. Then, effect. What do Romeo's last words show? My answer: Romeo's last words show that he dies loving Juliet, joining a kiss and death, while believing she is dead only moments before she wakes; his final act completes the play's link between passion and death.

middleSchool.note: Excerpt-based: read the passage aloud first; use the scaffolds; accept partial answers and build with probes.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

contentNotes.teacherNote: Romeo dies by poison and Juliet by a dagger; Paris is killed. Use the safe-messaging script; discuss the Prince's verdict and the waste of young lives, not methods. This section mentions drinking or a drug (“…ison, I see, hath been his timeless end: O churl! drunk all, and left no friendly drop To help…”). Treat it as period custom or plot detail; name it plainly and don't glamorize it.
contentNotes.studentPreview: The ending shows three deaths, two by suicide. Support is available if this is hard to read.

safeMessaging.teacherScript: Discuss the character's despair and what the text does with it; do not dwell on methods.
